lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Daisy, it's Ana. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Ana. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about swimming instead of walking.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your body feeling this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay. The heat is getting to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to walk 15 minutes on 5 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it! 5 out of 5 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're really honest with yourself, and that helps.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: With all the rain I just stayed in.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It rained almost every afternoon.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, yes. My knees have been bothering me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to move more, but not if it means hurting yourself.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walking going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've picked your days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You need to walk every day, no excuses.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: When I walk I sleep better, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you use the step counter?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've already started.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Just get out there, even when it's hot.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I walk 20 minutes on 5 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 6.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 6 and not a 3?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Getting back to work is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If taking care of everybody gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: taking care of everybody made this week harder, you still got 5 days in, and your plan is to walk 20 minutes on 5 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Daisy, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Reflects ambivalence and desire to keep going
Knee discomfort as barrier; minor symptom
Reflects desire balanced with safety worry
Asks how she wants to proceed
Asks what would make it easier
Desire to feel like herself again
Reflects openness and need for fit
Took a concrete step: fridge reminder

flags.reason: 'You need to walk every day, no excuses' is directive and undercuts autonomy; not MI-consistent.
Health-threat warning without permission; likely to increase resistance.
'Just get out there, even when it's hot' pushes despite heat and knee barriers she raised.
Participant noticed better sleep from walking; coach did not explore or reinforce this motivation.
Knee pain raised as barrier; coach moved past it instead of exploring safe activity options.

score.summary: Ana used good reflections and affirmations early and built a clear 20-minute, 5-day goal with a rainy-day backup. However, she slipped into directive statements ('no excuses', health warnings, 'just get out there') that conflicted with her autonomy-supporting language.
strengths: Line 10 and 34: affirmed Daisy's honesty and progress specifically.
Line 25 and 39: complex reflections captured the wish to move alongside the need to protect her body.
Line 64: clear summary before closing, and Daisy confirmed it.
coaching_tips: Line 37 and 50: replace directives with a reflection or question, such as 'What feels doable in this heat?'
Line 46: avoid health warnings; instead ask 'What do you already know about how activity helps you?'
Line 41: explore the sleep benefit she noticed, e.g., 'What's it like noticing better sleep?'
Line 24: when knee pain comes up, ask permission before suggesting options and check for any pain that needs medical attention.
Line 19: offering the mall idea with 'Do you mind if I tell you' was good; keep offering ideas this way.
